title: Open a manikin's airway with an oral airway without pushing the tongue back
instruction: Open the manikin's airway with the green oral airway so its flange rests at the lips, then let go.
context: Insert a curved tool upside down and turn it at depth, so its tip sweeps under a sprung soft obstacle and lifts it instead of pushing it back. EMTs, paramedics (O*NET 29-2042.00, 29-2043.00) and respiratory therapists (29-1126.00) do this with an oropharyngeal (Guedel) airway in every unconscious adult whose tongue blocks the throat. The curve must end behind the tongue base. Pushed straight in the way it finally sits, the tip lands on the tongue and shoves it into the throat, the failure the technique exists to prevent. The turn is not a lock or a fastening: it is what moves the tongue. Holding the jaw open with the other hand is only the enabling role.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. (1) Airway-trainer head: an adult-length trainer whose mouth cavity and tongue are about 1.6x adult width, skin-tone vinyl over rigid foam, colour sRGB (0.87, 0.72, 0.62), 2.0 kg, fixed to the table face up. Footprint 200 x 150 mm centred at (0.178, -0.036); 80 mm from the table to the lips (98 mm to the nose tip); lips centred at (0.170, -0.030, 0.8275). The chin points along world yaw 142 deg (back toward the left arm), the top of the head forward and right. Inside the mouth: a cavity 94 mm long, 80 mm wide and 52 mm deep under the lips; the back wall of the throat is 64 mm below the lips. Inner surfaces are wet: friction 0.3 static / 0.25 dynamic. (2) Lower jaw (part of the head): a hinged vinyl mandible shell, 0.10 kg, same colour, friction 0.9 / 0.8: a 20 x 43 x 10 mm lower lip and teeth bar and a 24 x 50 x 10 mm chin plate (centre (0.156, -0.019, 0.8205)), on a horizontal hinge 72 mm below the lips at (0.182, -0.039, 0.7555) across the head. A torsion spring (0.3 N m/rad) holds it shut with no gap between the lips and a 0.04 N m net preload; it opens to 35 deg (28 deg gives a 33 mm mouth). (3) Tongue base (part of the head): a pink silicone insert, sRGB (0.85, 0.45, 0.50), wet (friction 0.15 / 0.10), 25 g, 72 mm wide and 40 x 19 mm in profile, on a horizontal hinge at (0.137, -0.004, 0.7775), 50 mm below the lips; its front-lower face is a 31 deg ramp facing the top of the head. A 0.025 N m/rad spring (its rest offset cancels the insert's weight) holds its base 2 mm above the back wall of the throat; pressed 6.7 deg back it touches the wall; it lifts forward up to 42 deg. (4) Oral airway: a green Guedel-pattern oropharyngeal airway, size 2 (80 mm), PVC, sRGB (0.15, 0.65, 0.30), friction 0.4 / 0.3, 12 g: a 56 x 22 x 7 mm flange, a 31 mm bite block of 16 x 10 mm stadium section, and a 90 deg curve of 28 mm centreline radius, 16 x 10 mm in section, 82 mm from the flange top to the tip along its centreline; seated with its flange on the lips, the end of its curve rests on the back wall of the throat. It hangs flange-up in the tray pocket, flange-bottom centre at (0.240, -0.210, 0.828), its curve pointing along world yaw 142 deg (the way it finally sits). (5) Airway kit tray: grey ABS, sRGB (0.55, 0.57, 0.60), 0.3 kg, fixed: a 74 x 46 x 80 mm block centred at (0.234, -0.205) at yaw 142 deg, with an open pocket 60 x 32 mm and 72 mm deep along the airway's curve; the airway's flange bridges the pocket's long rims.
scoring: Measured in the head frame (u toward the chin, w up, mm from the lip centre) every control step from reset; q_t = tongue angle (+ pushed back toward the throat), gap = tongue base's lowest edge above the back wall (2.0 at rest), q_j = jaw opening. Whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step and cleared only by the simulator reset, so pulling the airway out and starting again never clears it). Gate, any time in the run, gives 0: the tongue base pushed back 3.0 deg or more (its 2 mm rest gap to the throat wall closed to 0.7 mm). Any push-back means the tip rode on top of the tongue, the failure the technique exists to prevent; 3 deg sits clear of contact jitter (the demo peaks at 0.0 deg) and reads on the tongue-hinge protractor. Seated: flange-bottom centre at most 4 mm above the lips and within 8 mm of its place, bite block within 15 deg of upright. Open airway: seated with the curve within 25 deg of pointing at the chin, the tongue lifted at least 15 deg, its base at least 8 mm off the wall, and the airway's tip at least 5 mm past the tongue's front edge. Ladder: 0.25 = the held airway's tip went 35 mm into the open mouth (jaw 10 deg or more), any technique; 0.5 = with the airway in the mouth the tongue was lifted 10 deg at some time; 0.75 = open airway at the end; 1.0 = open airway at the end with the jaw closed onto the bite block (12 deg or less), the airway still (under 3 mm/s and 3 deg/s, from its pose change between control steps) for 2 s, and the release gate: every pad of both grippers at least 30 mm from the head, jaw, tongue and airway and both grippers moving under 5 mm/s for the last 1 s. Success (1.0) must hold 1 s. Real trial: a top photo for the flange at the lips and its direction; the video for stillness; a side cut-away view (the trainer's clear cheek panel) with a mm scale for the tongue base's gap to the throat wall; a protractor on the jaw and tongue hinges.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Take the airway out and hang it flange-up in the tray pocket with its curve pointing toward the head's chin side (world yaw 142 deg). Let the jaw spring shut the mouth (0 deg, lips touching) and check the tongue insert rests with its base 2 mm above the throat wall (a 2 mm feeler gauge through the clear cheek panel). Re-wet the inner surfaces with the trainer's lubricant spray. The head and the tray are fixed on taped outlines and need no reset.
fidelity: Rigid trainer: a fixed skull, a sprung hinged jaw and one sprung hinged tongue-base wedge (a real tongue is soft and joined to the jaw). The cavity and tongue are about 1.6x adult width and the lips 80 mm above the table (about 180 in life), so the rigid airway can turn where tissue would yield. Joint stops stand in for the throat wall and the closed bite. Wet inner surfaces and a light tongue spring (0.025 N m/rad).
